# Installer Evidence Checklist: Windows Installer Identity and Verification

**Purpose**: Validate that the requirements distinguish durable package
contracts from clean-environment observations and define the complete Windows
install lifecycle evidence expected by reviewers.
**Created**: 2026-08-27
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based
on feature context and requirements.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are both installer-created identity surfaces named explicitly? [Completeness, Spec §User Story 1]
- [x] CHK002 Is the running GUI identity requirement defined separately from installer-created surfaces? [Completeness, Spec §User Story 2]
- [x] CHK003 Are install, new-shell use, reinstall or upgrade, and uninstall all included in the search-path lifecycle? [Completeness, Spec §User Story 3]
- [x] CHK004 Is the canonical icon asset relationship specified for every surface in scope? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001–FR-004]
- [x] CHK005 Are maintainer-check failure classes enumerated for icon and search-path drift? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006–FR-009]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK006 Is a clean environment distinguished unambiguously from a development machine with a prior install or search-path entry? [Clarity, Spec §User Story 3]
- [x] CHK007 Is a newly opened shell distinguished from an already-open shell that inherited stale environment state? [Clarity, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK008 Is the generic Explorer icon for the `.msi` file explicitly excluded from the installed-product icon requirements? [Clarity, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK009 Is “official brand mark” tied to one canonical existing asset rather than an undefined visual preference? [Clarity, Spec §Key Entities]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK010 Do the icon requirements consistently require one canonical asset for Start Menu, installed-apps, and GUI-artifact relationships? [Consistency, Spec §FR-001–FR-004]
- [x] CHK011 Do issue-closure requirements agree with the distinction among definition, candidate-artifact, published-artifact, and native observation evidence? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011–FR-012]
- [x] CHK012 Do lifecycle requirements preserve the existing per-machine scope and unrelated search-path entries? [Consistency, Spec §FR-005, FR-014]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK013 Can each protected installer relationship be evaluated independently with a specific expected failure? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002]
- [x] CHK014 Is complete lifecycle-procedure coverage expressed as a countable outcome? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004]
- [x] CHK015 Is every scoped issue required to carry an explicit proven, failed, or unavailable status? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005]
- [x] CHK016 Is repository-wide completion tied to the existing eight named quality gates? [Measurability, Spec §SC-007]

## Scenario and Edge-Case Coverage

- [x] CHK017 Are stale icon-cache behavior and the acceptable refresh boundary addressed without treating cache refresh as a product repair? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 2]
- [x] CHK018 Are duplicate search-path entries and malformed empty segments covered during reinstall and uninstall? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 3]
- [x] CHK019 Is the unavailable-clean-environment outcome defined without allowing it to count as a pass? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 4]
- [x] CHK020 Are release publication, host virtualization changes, signing, bootstrap executables, and brand redesign explicitly outside scope? [Coverage, Spec §FR-013, Assumptions]

## Dependencies and Assumptions

- [x] CHK021 Is the published-artifact dependency for issue #16 stated explicitly? [Dependency, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK022 Is the need for a disposable or genuinely clean Windows environment documented? [Dependency, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK023 Is the current host’s inability to provide clean evidence recorded without generalizing it into a product failure? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK024 Is native visual observation kept distinct from static package-definition evidence? [Dependency, Spec §FR-010–FR-012]

## Notes

- Standard-depth checklist for the author and PR reviewers.
- All 24 requirements-quality checks pass. Native verification may still be
  unavailable during implementation; that is an execution status governed by
  FR-011 and FR-012, not a gap in the written requirements.
